units.rhetorical_move: opens by naming the concern as growing
units.function: frames the problem as something the world has come to worry about

original_instantiations: a two decade span is cited so the worry reads as established rather than new
the concern is attributed to the whole world, not to the authors

units.source_excerpt: has become more and more concerned by the whole world
units.reusable_pattern: a growing concern can be dated and then attributed to everyone
reusable_elements: the attribution to the whole world
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the doubled comparative for every trend

units.rhetorical_move: names the model and its parent in one breath
units.function: a new model is introduced as an extension of a known one

original_instantiations: the new model is named and its known parent is named in the same sentence
the extension is called significant before any result is shown

units.source_excerpt: a novel model called PSA, which is significantly extended from the well-known PSR model
units.reusable_pattern: introduce a model by naming what it extends
prohibited_generalizations: do not call every modification significant

units.rhetorical_move: holds one input fixed to remove an effect
units.function: a counterfactual is built by freezing the relevant inputs

original_instantiations: the curve without the effect is made by holding the climate inputs at fixed values
the counterfactual is defined by what is kept constant, not by a new model

units.source_excerpt: the FI curve without the effect of climate changes is modeled by keeping the values of the corresponding climate indicators constant
units.reusable_pattern: remove an effect by holding its inputs constant
prohibited_generalizations: do not freeze inputs without saying which ones

units.rhetorical_move: reports a crossing year
units.function: a forecast is stated as the year a threshold is reached

original_instantiations: the forecast is reported as the year the country is likely to cross into stable
the hedge likely sits inside the year claim

units.source_excerpt: the time that BD is likely to become a stable state is around 2076
units.reusable_pattern: state a forecast as a crossing year
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the hedge from a long forecast

units.rhetorical_move: recommends one policy and prices its growth
units.function: a finding becomes a spending rule

features.quantitative_role: thirty five percent every five years
original_instantiations: the disasters are called serious and the spending on one intervention is told to rise by a fixed share
the recommendation names the intervention by number

units.source_excerpt: natural disasters are serious and we suggest investing more, and this expenditure will increase by 35% every 5 years
units.reusable_pattern: turn a finding into a fixed growth rule for spending
reusable_elements: the growth rate and its period
prohibited_generalizations: do not invent a growth rate the paper does not give

units.rhetorical_move: closes on a promise of deep understanding
units.function: the sensitivity is framed as understanding rather than as a test

original_instantiations: the sensitivity analysis is said to give a deep understanding of the model
the report ends by discussing strengths and weaknesses

units.source_excerpt: we conduct a sensitivity analysis in order to gain some deep understanding of our model
units.reusable_pattern: frame a sensitivity test as a search for understanding
prohibited_generalizations: do not promise depth the test does not deliver

units.rhetorical_move: chains causes into a cascade
units.function: one cause is walked through several consequences to a conflict

original_instantiations: warming is followed through extreme weather to shortages and then to famine and disease
each step uses the same verb so the chain reads as inevitable

units.source_excerpt: the climate change leads to more frequent drought and flood, and leads to decline of water, food and energy, and then even leads to famine and diseases
units.reusable_pattern: build a causal chain by repeating one verb
prohibited_generalizations: do not stack leads-to without a real chain

units.rhetorical_move: escalates from inability to war
units.function: a government's failure is extended to outside interference and then to war

original_instantiations: the failure to handle famine is followed by local conflict and then by outside interference and war
two conditionals are stacked so the worst case arrives last

units.source_excerpt: if the government is unable to solve the problem there will be local violent conflicts, and if a foreign government interferes there will be wars
units.reusable_pattern: escalate a domestic failure into an international one with stacked conditionals
prohibited_generalizations: do not add an outside actor the paper does not

units.rhetorical_move: closes the background on unprecedented significance
units.function: the stakes are raised to their highest at the end of the section

original_instantiations: the chain ends by calling the task significant beyond any precedent
the superlative is saved for the last sentence

units.source_excerpt: reducing the fragility of a state has its unprecedented significance in today's world
units.reusable_pattern: end a background by raising the stakes to a superlative
prohibited_generalizations: do not use unprecedented for an ordinary claim

units.rhetorical_move: lists the tasks as things to be accomplished
units.function: the problem is restated as a list of tasks

original_instantiations: the goal of a more stable world is followed by the tasks that must be done
each task points back to a numbered task in the prompt

units.source_excerpt: to create a more stable world, fragile state should be studied first and the following tasks are to be accomplished
units.reusable_pattern: restate a problem as a numbered list of tasks
prohibited_generalizations: do not restate tasks the prompt does not set

units.rhetorical_move: claims the model is rational because the rankings agree
units.function: agreement with a known ranking is taken as proof of reasonableness

original_instantiations: the result is set against a published ranking and the model is then called rational
the verdict follows in the same sentence as the comparison

units.source_excerpt: we compare the result with the ranking and discover that our model is rational
units.reusable_pattern: treat agreement with a known ranking as a verdict on the model
prohibited_generalizations: do not equate agreement with correctness

units.rhetorical_move: defines a tipping point as a number
units.function: a threshold is declared by fiat inside the roadmap

original_instantiations: a tipping point is set at a round number and tied back to the task range
the forecast method is named right after the threshold

units.source_excerpt: according to the range in the task, we define a tipping point 0.6 and forecast the time taken to reach that point
units.reusable_pattern: declare a tipping point as a round number before forecasting it
prohibited_generalizations: do not present a chosen round number as a derived one

units.rhetorical_move: assumes the countries are regular
units.function: an assumption is stated in one line and justified in the next

original_instantiations: the countries are assumed to follow regular patterns, and the reason given is that this matches the facts
the justification is a single clause

units.source_excerpt: we assume the countries we studied are regular, since almost every country's development conforms to certain regular patterns, which is based on facts
units.reusable_pattern: state an assumption and justify it in the same breath
prohibited_generalizations: do not ground an assumption on facts that are not named

units.rhetorical_move: defends an assumption as avoiding trouble
units.function: an assumption is justified by the trouble it saves

original_instantiations: the assumption is called reasonable because the study focuses on climate and wants to avoid trouble
the convenience is stated openly

units.source_excerpt: we focus more on climate change, thus this assumption is reasonable and helps avoid unnecessary troubles
units.reusable_pattern: justify an assumption by the trouble it avoids
prohibited_generalizations: do not hide a convenience argument as a factual one

units.rhetorical_move: assumes everything not studied is uninfluential
units.function: the unmodeled factors are dismissed in one sentence

original_instantiations: the large number of other indicators is conceded and then all of them are called uninfluential
the dismissal covers everything not listed

units.source_excerpt: there are large numbers of indicators, thus we assume that other indicators except those mentioned are uninfluential
units.reusable_pattern: dismiss every unlisted factor in one clause
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim unlisted factors are negligible without a reason

units.rhetorical_move: trusts the sources because they are authoritative
units.function: data quality is assumed from the authority of the websites

original_instantiations: the statistics are called precise because the websites are authoritative
the verdict repeats the word reasonable

units.source_excerpt: the statistics we collected are from different websites which are authoritative, therefore this assumption is reasonable
units.reusable_pattern: treat an authoritative source as a precise one
prohibited_generalizations: do not equate authority with accuracy

units.rhetorical_move: points at the table
units.function: the notation is handed to a table

original_instantiations: the reader is sent to a table for the symbols
no symbol is defined in the sentence itself

units.source_excerpt: symbols that we use in the model are shown in the following table
units.reusable_pattern: hand the notation to a table
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave a symbol undefined in both prose and table

units.rhetorical_move: fills gaps with a named procedure
units.function: missing values are filled and the reason is smoothness

original_instantiations: missing statistics are filled by a named imputation so the later analysis runs smoothly
the software is named

units.source_excerpt: we utilize multiple imputation to fill the missing values to ensure smooth data processing and analysis
units.reusable_pattern: name the imputation and the reason for using it
prohibited_generalizations: do not fill missing data without saying so

units.rhetorical_move: defines each letter of a known model
units.function: a borrowed model is unpacked letter by letter

original_instantiations: each letter of the borrowed model is given its meaning in turn
the authors add their own reading of the pressure letter

units.source_excerpt: in the model, P represents the pressure dimension, which indicates the pressure brought to the system
units.reusable_pattern: unpack a borrowed model's name letter by letter
prohibited_generalizations: do not change a borrowed definition silently

units.rhetorical_move: assigns each dimension its source
units.function: each group of indicators is traced to a source

original_instantiations: the pressure indicators are assumed, the sensitivity ones are taken from a cited study, and the adaptation ones from a published index
three sources are named for three groups

units.source_excerpt: as for sensitivity, we determine indicators according to one cited study, and finally we choose indicators for adaptation referring to a published index
units.reusable_pattern: give each indicator group its own source
prohibited_generalizations: do not cite a source for indicators it does not contain

units.rhetorical_move: reads an indicator as a comparative
units.function: an indicator is glossed as a bigger-means-worse sentence

original_instantiations: a higher density is read as a heavier burden on resources and on infrastructure
the gloss has no formula

units.source_excerpt: the higher the population density, the heavier the burden on national resources and on public infrastructure
units.reusable_pattern: gloss an indicator with a comparative chain
prohibited_generalizations: do not state a direction the data does not support

units.rhetorical_move: sorts indicators into three marked types
units.function: the direction of each indicator is named with a symbol

original_instantiations: the indicators are split into bigger is better, smaller is better, and closer to a value
each case gets its own mark

units.source_excerpt: we find that the indicators can be divided into three types: bigger is better, smaller is better, and better when closer to a specific value
units.reusable_pattern: classify indicators by the direction of better
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave an indicator's direction unmarked

units.rhetorical_move: introduces a formula with a therefore
units.function: the formula is presented as the consequence of the classification

original_instantiations: the bigger-is-better case is followed by the formula that should be used
the obligation word attaches to the equation

units.source_excerpt: therefore, for those bigger is better, the equation should be
units.reusable_pattern: lead into a formula with an obligation word
prohibited_generalizations: do not say an equation should be used when several fit

units.rhetorical_move: concedes a known flaw with as we all know
units.function: a method's weakness is stated as common knowledge

original_instantiations: the judgment method's subjectivity is called common knowledge and the entropy method is brought in to answer it
the remedy follows the concession directly

units.source_excerpt: as we all know, the hierarchy method has some subjectivity due to the score matrices, hence we calculate the weights another way
units.reusable_pattern: concede a method's flaw as common knowledge before replacing it
prohibited_generalizations: do not call a flaw common knowledge without naming it

units.rhetorical_move: states the blend shares as a supposition
units.function: the mixing constants are presented as a supposition

original_instantiations: the judgment share is set at most of the weight and the entropy share at the rest
the numbers are introduced with suppose

units.source_excerpt: since we want to reduce the subjectivity, we take a weighted average, and here we suppose the two shares are 0.8 and 0.2
units.reusable_pattern: present mixing constants as an explicit supposition
prohibited_generalizations: do not hide a chosen share as a derived one

units.rhetorical_move: separates direct from indirect effects
units.function: the same cause is split into direct and indirect routes

original_instantiations: temperature and sea level are called direct, while forests, crops and health are called indirect
each route gets its own headed list

units.source_excerpt: through direct means the temperature departure and the sea level make a state more fragile, and through indirect means the forests, crops and health decline
units.reusable_pattern: split one cause into a direct list and an indirect list
prohibited_generalizations: do not call an effect direct without a mechanism

units.rhetorical_move: escalates with what's worse
units.function: a consequence chain peaks at total loss

original_instantiations: the crop losses are followed by the worse case of no harvest at all
the escalation marker does the work of a new paragraph

units.source_excerpt: the increased temperature brings insects and pathogens and death in batches, and what is worse, there will be no harvest at all
units.reusable_pattern: mark the worst step of a chain with an escalation phrase
prohibited_generalizations: do not escalate past what the source supports

units.rhetorical_move: reads a figure as consistent with a trend
units.function: visual agreement is taken as reasonableness

original_instantiations: the figure is said to follow the ranking's trend and the model is called reasonable
the verdict word is misspelled and kept

units.source_excerpt: we can clearly see that the result is relatively consistent with the trend of the ranking, and for this reason we believe the model is reasonable
units.reusable_pattern: read a figure's agreement with a ranking as a verdict
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat a visual match as validation

units.rhetorical_move: turns an inequality into a label
units.function: a band is applied by stating the inequality and the label together

original_instantiations: crossing one inequality is said to make the state stable
the conclusion is drawn in the same sentence

units.source_excerpt: when the index of a state satisfies the inequality, we can draw a conclusion that the state is stable
units.reusable_pattern: attach a label to an inequality in one sentence
prohibited_generalizations: do not state a band edge the paper does not print

units.rhetorical_move: claims validity from mostly consistent
units.function: partial agreement is promoted to validity

original_instantiations: the classification mostly matches a published one and this is called proof of validity
the hedge mostly is kept

units.source_excerpt: our model's classification results are mostly consistent with the published index, which proves that our model is valid
units.reusable_pattern: promote a partial match to a proof
prohibited_generalizations: do not call a partial match a proof

units.rhetorical_move: explains a dip with a dated event
units.function: a move in the curve is pinned to a named event

original_instantiations: the fall in the index is traced to a disease outbreak and then to the rainstorm behind it
the event is dated and sourced

units.source_excerpt: the reason for the decrease of the index is the outbreak at the end of the year, which put a million people at risk
units.reusable_pattern: explain a move in a curve by a dated event
prohibited_generalizations: do not attach an event that falls outside the dip

units.rhetorical_move: names the two curves by color
units.function: a counterfactual and a baseline are distinguished by color and by name

original_instantiations: the curve without the effect and the curve with it are each given a color and a short name
the names are used again later

units.source_excerpt: the red curve represents the index without the effects and is denoted one way, and the blue curve represents the index with the effects
units.reusable_pattern: distinguish a counterfactual curve by color and by name
prohibited_generalizations: do not refer to a curve color the figure does not use

units.rhetorical_move: reads a slow rise as a suggestion
units.function: a curve's shape is interpreted cautiously

original_instantiations: a slow upward curve is read as the country becoming less fragile once the effect is removed
the verb is suggest, not show

units.source_excerpt: the curve shows a slow uptrend, which suggests the country will be less fragile without the effects
units.reusable_pattern: hedge a curve reading with a weak verb
prohibited_generalizations: do not upgrade a suggestion to a finding

units.rhetorical_move: offers an alternative cause
units.function: a residual rise is handed to other factors

original_instantiations: the index still rises after the climate effect is removed, and other factors are offered as the cause
the alternative is hedged

units.source_excerpt: the index still rises slowly and even stagnates, and it is possible that the country is affected by other factors
units.reusable_pattern: explain a residual with a hedged alternative cause
prohibited_generalizations: do not assert an alternative cause as fact

units.rhetorical_move: states the forecast twice, in years and in a date
units.function: a horizon is given both as a span and as a calendar year

original_instantiations: the country is said to be stable in sixty years, and that is restated as a calendar year
the restatement uses namely

units.source_excerpt: the country will be stable in 60 years, namely 2076
units.reusable_pattern: give a forecast both as a span and as a year
prohibited_generalizations: do not compute the year wrongly

units.rhetorical_move: sets constraints before predicting
units.function: a forecast is fenced by stated constraints

original_instantiations: the spending forecast is bounded by three stated constraints before any number appears
one constraint fixes a single intervention's growth

units.source_excerpt: we set up constraint conditions when predicting the total cost
units.reusable_pattern: fence a forecast with explicit constraints
prohibited_generalizations: do not add a constraint the paper does not state

units.rhetorical_move: replaces an indicator with a similar one
units.function: a model is moved to a new scale by swapping indicators

original_instantiations: indicators that a city cannot supply are replaced by similar ones
each swap pairs the missing indicator with its stand in

units.source_excerpt: it is difficult to evaluate one indicator for a city, so we use a similar one instead, and another barrier is replaced the same way
units.reusable_pattern: adapt a model to a new scale by swapping indicators for similar ones
prohibited_generalizations: do not swap an indicator for an unrelated one

units.rhetorical_move: reads a table as reasonable
units.function: a three row table is enough for a verdict

original_instantiations: the highest and lowest of three continent scores are read off and the result is called reasonable
the verdict rests on a map

units.source_excerpt: we can clearly see that one continent gets the highest score and another the lowest, and our result is reasonable
units.reusable_pattern: draw a verdict from the order of a small table
prohibited_generalizations: do not call a three value table a validation

units.rhetorical_move: reads unchanged trend as stability
units.function: robustness is argued from a trend that barely moves

original_instantiations: the mixing share is moved through several values and the trend is said to change little, so the model is called stable
the verdict equates a stable trend with a stable model

units.source_excerpt: when the value is changing, the trend does not change a lot, which means the model is stable
units.reusable_pattern: call a model stable when its trend barely moves
prohibited_generalizations: do not infer model stability from one parameter

units.rhetorical_move: claims the blend covers both methods' faults
units.function: a strength is stated as fixing two named faults

original_instantiations: the blend is said to supply the comparison one method lacks and to reduce the subjectivity of the other
the hedge to some extent guards the claim

units.source_excerpt: to some extent, this method supplies the comparison one method lacks and reduces the subjectivity of the other
units.reusable_pattern: state a strength as the fixing of two named faults
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim a fault is fixed when it is only reduced

units.rhetorical_move: owns a shortcut and its deviation
units.function: a weakness is stated as a shortcut taken under time pressure

original_instantiations: the continent score is admitted to be an average of a few countries, taken because time was short, and a deviation is conceded
the cause and the consequence are both owned

units.source_excerpt: due to time constraints, we just choose the average of some states to represent the continent, thus there will be some deviation
units.reusable_pattern: own a shortcut and name the error it causes
prohibited_generalizations: do not bury a shortcut in the method section

units.rhetorical_move: states where the model stops being reliable
units.function: a limitation is given as a condition of failure

original_instantiations: wars and riots are left out, and the model is then called unreliable for countries in large scale war
the boundary is stated as a condition

units.source_excerpt: we do not take riots and wars into consideration, therefore our model is not reliable when facing states with large scale wars
units.reusable_pattern: state a limitation as the condition under which the model fails
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim reliability outside the stated condition

units.rhetorical_move: stacks the achievements in one paragraph
units.function: the close repeats the whole pipeline in order

original_instantiations: the score, the two countries, the spending, the extension and the sensitivity are listed in the order they were done
each clause is one stage

units.source_excerpt: we measure fragility, analyze the two countries, estimate the spending, extend the model to cities and continents, and find it stable
units.reusable_pattern: close by repeating the pipeline in order
prohibited_generalizations: do not add a stage the paper did not do

units.rhetorical_move: mixes guide, data page and news report
units.function: the source list runs from reference works to news

original_instantiations: the list holds a topic guide, data catalogues, a scenario report and news pages
each entry stands on its own numbered line

units.source_excerpt: the sources run from a topic guide and data catalogues to news reports
units.reusable_pattern: let the reference list show the range of source types
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat a news page as a dataset

units.rhetorical_move: lists every country with its score and its rank
units.function: the full result is given as a table

original_instantiations: each country is given its score and its rank on the published list
the table is the only content of the appendix

units.source_excerpt: the appendix lists each country with its score and its rank on the published index
units.reusable_pattern: put the full result in an appendix table
prohibited_generalizations: do not recompute a rank the table does not show
